t: A nomadic people of the Gansu corridor, strong enough in the 3rd century BCE to hold the Xiongnu prince Modu hostage.
Defeated by the Xiongnu, they migrated west to the Ili valley and then took Bactria, probably in the 130s BCE.
Zhang Qian's mission to them opened Han China to the West, and their Guishuang chiefs founded the Kushan Empire.
dyk: The Xiongnu turned the skull of a defeated Yuezhi king into a drinking cup; according to the Han shu, Han envoys later drank from it when swearing a blood oath with a Xiongnu chanyu.
ev: Modu, once a hostage of the Yuezhi, seizes power among the Xiongnu
The Xiongnu defeat the Yuezhi in the Gansu corridor
The Greater Yuezhi move west and drive the Saka from the Ili valley
The Wusun expel the Yuezhi, who move south and take Bactria
The Han envoy Zhang Qian reaches the Yuezhi court
Kujula Kadphises unites the five xihou and founds the Kushan Empire

f.capital: Nomadic; later a court north of the Amu Darya (Jianshi)
